title: When the Ghost Falls
premise: Marguerite Coldharbour, a private security contractor who has spent a decade erasing her past as an intelligence asset, is approached by a stranger claiming she owes him for a rescue that never happened. The debt is real, however: it was incurred by the woman whose identity Marguerite stole after a botched operation left her original self dead on paper. The stranger, a fixer named Ansel Voss, demands payment in kind—Marguerite must infiltrate the security detail of a tech summit to stop a sabotage plot designed to kill hundreds while reading as a tragic accident. As she unravels the conspiracy, she discovers her former handler orchestrated both the attack and her exposure, forcing her to choose between vanishing again and standing in the open to testify. In the end, Marguerite stops the attack at devastating personal cost, surrenders her false identity to the authorities, and accepts that survival bought with invisibility was never truly living.
about_author: Jude Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent fifteen years advising corporations on threat mitigation across three continents before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town they refuse to name, drawing on a career spent around people whose job titles never matched their work.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet her mid-contract, guarding a paranoid fintech executive through a hostile shareholder meeting. Her routines—go-bag by the door, three exit routes memorized, lie about her past polished smooth—establish her discipline and isolation. Beat: controlled competence masking chronic fear of exposure.

chapters.title: A Favor Returned
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A man named Ansel Voss appears at her apartment with details no stranger should know: a rescue in Marseilles eleven years ago that saved 'her' life. She knows the rescue happened—to someone else. He gives her seventy-two hours. Beat: the floor tilts; her constructed life cracks.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a flashback to the botched operation where the real Marguerite Coldharbour died and our narrator took her identity. She digs into her own forged history and finds it has been edited recently—by professionals. Beat: dread deepening into certainty that someone is dismantling her cover deliberately.

chapters.title: Terms of Debt
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Confronting Voss, she learns the truth: he knew the original Coldharbour, and his demand is leverage—he'll expose the identity theft unless she takes a job. The target: security lead for the Meridian Summit, where forty delegates will convene in three weeks. Beat: cornered fury; she agrees to gather evidence against him instead.

chapters.title: Inside the Wire
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Using her reputation, she maneuvers onto the summit security team under a legitimate contract, meeting her new client, summit director Elena Vasquez, and rival contractor Dale Pruitt. She begins quietly investigating Voss's network. Beat: cautious re-entry into the world she swore off, adrenaline sharpening her focus.

chapters.title: What the Cameras Miss
chapters.summary: Pruitt's POV. The rival contractor notices anomalies in the venue's HVAC maintenance logs—contractors with thin histories—and starts his own inquiry, suspicious of everyone including Marguerite. Beat: paranoia from the outside looking in; the reader sees the plot's edges before Marguerite does.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A burner call comes from Marcus Hale, her former intelligence handler, offering to make Voss disappear if she walks away from the summit. His voice triggers old conditioning—and old suspicion. She records the call. Beat: the past reaching forward; trust in nothing, least of herself.

chapters.title: Accident Architecture
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. We see the conspiracy's mechanics: a rigged cooling system failure timed to the summit's opening gala, designed to read as infrastructure decay. Voss believes he's working for a whistleblower faction; hints suggest his employers are not what he thinks. Beat: dramatic irony tightening—the reader knows more than either protagonist.

chapters.title: Two Liars at Dinner
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She engineers a dinner with Voss, playing confession to extract names. He reveals a fragment she didn't expect: the original Marguerite Coldharbour may not have died in the operation—she was murdered, and Hale signed the order. Beat: grief detonating under the professional mask; the mission turns personal.

chapters.title: Pruitt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Pruitt's POV. Pruitt confronts Marguerite with his findings, offering an uneasy alliance—or blackmail. She flips him by showing him the sabotage evidence she's assembled; his contractor's code chooses the paycheck over the principle. Beat: reluctant partnership forged from mutual distrust.

chapters.title: The Middle Floor
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Following the HVAC thread into the venue's sub-levels, she finds modified dampers and a dead technician's ID badge—one belonging to a man she recognizes from her old unit. Someone inside her former world is running the op. Beat: cold clarity; the attack is real, scheduled, and insider-built.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Elena Vasquez's POV. Vasquez receives an anonymous dossier questioning Marguerite's credentials—Hale's countermove. She suspends Marguerite pending review, gutting her access days before the summit. Beat: betrayal and helplessness; the walls closing from every direction at once.

chapters.title: Ghosts Negotiating
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Desperate, she meets Hale face-to-face and lays out what she knows, offering silence for the truth about the original Coldharbour. Hale neither confirms nor denies—but his micro-reactions tell her enough. Beat: a duel of composure; she leaves knowing Hale is protecting the operation, not hunting it.

chapters.title: Voss Learns the Price
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss discovers his paymaster is Hale's cutout, meaning he's been a deniable asset all along—and that his own name sits on the accident's casualty contingency list. He reaches out to Marguerite, hat in hand. Beat: the manipulator manipulated; pride collapsing into survival instinct.

chapters.title: Reentry by Force
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Voss's alternating POV. With Pruitt's help, they engineer Marguerite's reinstatement by feeding Vasquez verifiable sabotage evidence—sacrificing secrecy for access. Vasquez, convinced, brings her back but puts her on a short leash. Beat: risky alliance cemented; the clock now runs in hours, not days.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Countdown structure: the team maps the full plan—coolant breach during the gala, exits sealed by a staged fire alarm, blame pre-assigned to a dead patsy. They identify the trigger man: a former colleague Marguerite once saved. Beat: moral weight landing; stopping it means confronting her own history of debts.

chapters.title: The Man She Saved
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes's POV. The trigger man, torn between loyalty to Marguerite and threats against his family, prepares his end of the operation. A late-night call from Marguerite offers him a way out—if he trusts the woman who abandoned him once before. Beat: compassion inside the machinery; a human being deciding whether to be a weapon.

chapters.title: Gala Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The summit opens. Marguerite works the floor while Pruitt watches the plant rooms and Voss feeds her timing updates. Everything holds—too well. Then the fire alarm test fires early, off-schedule, wrong. Beat: coiled tension snapping taut; the plan is moving without its script.

chapters.title: When the Ghost Falls
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax. Hale, exposed by Vasquez's own audit, tries to accelerate the breach rather than lose it. Marguerite physically prevents the coolant release, Tomas refuses his trigger role, and Pruitt holds the stairwell against Hale's cleaners. Hale, cornered, nearly kills her—until Voss arrives and takes the bullet meant for her. Beat: everything paid at once; courage chosen over invisibility.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Aftermath: investigators descend, Vasquez testifies, and Marguerite makes her choice—she walks into a federal office and gives them her real name and the whole falsified one, accepting prosecution for identity theft in exchange for testimony against Hale's network. Beat: costly integrity; justice outside her control at last.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Plea proceedings, Hale's arrest, and the quiet burial of the original Marguerite Coldharbour's memory done properly this time. She serves a reduced sentence; Voss survives, crippled, and visits with grudging respect. Beat: reckoning without melodrama; the price itemized and paid.

chapters.title: One Bag, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue. Released, she takes honest work consulting on venue security under her true name—unremarkable, visible, accountable. The go-bag stays by the door out of habit, but for the first time she unpacks it, hangs the clothes in a closet, and sleeps with the window unlocked. Beat: hard-won peace; survival redefined as living seen.
